title: Composite Video on the NES: Why's it so wobbly?
summary: A technical deep-dive into why NES composite video output appears wobbly and fuzzy, explaining the underlying hardware limitations of the Picture Processing Unit (PPU) and how it generates composite video signals with inherent artifacts.
problem_solved: Explains why NES composite video exhibits color bleed, scanline artifacts, and wobbly pixels due to phase-altering color subcarrier timing issues.
why_valuable: Provides rare technical insight into retro gaming hardware quirks, helping emulator developers, hardware hackers, and enthusiasts understand why classic games look the way they do.
